open_points.subject: INV-020 Required test
open_points.text: “a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing” does not say how the test shows that accepted versions are never deleted or that every later version is appended rather than overwriting an earlier one.
open_points.question: What observations must the INV-020 test make to prove immutability, append-only versioning, and absence of deletion?
options: Exercise replay/conflict only and verify the existing snapshot is unchanged
Also create successive versions and verify all remain, and verify no operation or store surface can delete or overwrite an accepted snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Verify replay and conflict preserve the existing snapshot, successive versions coexist, and no deletion or replacement surface exists.

open_points.subject: INV-022 Required test
open_points.text: “a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing” does not say how that one test demonstrates both that import and activation are distinct actions and that a producer has no activation capability.
open_points.question: Which histories and observations must prove INV-022?
options: Only attempt activation as a producer and expect refusal
Also import as a producer and show the import leaves the version inactive until a separately authorized human activation
open_points.default_guess: Test both producer activation refusal and that successful import alone never activates a version.

open_points.subject: INV-023 Required test
open_points.text: “a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing” does not say what demonstrates atomic deactivation of the former active version or the absence of a commit point with two active versions.
open_points.question: What must the activation test observe to prove both uniqueness and atomic replacement of the active version?
options: Assert only that the final state has one active version
Also force a failure during activation and show the old version remains active with no partial deactivation or second activation
open_points.default_guess: Assert final uniqueness and rollback behavior under an injected failure in the activation transaction.

open_points.subject: INV-024 Required test
open_points.text: The single test at `upsert_manual_section_plan` is only described as “showing the invariant holds”; it does not state how it proves at most one manual version per project, active-project-only mutation, and immutability of imported plans.
open_points.question: Which cases must the INV-024 test cover?
options: Only reject an edit while the project is archived
Also attempt creation of a second manual version and mutation of an imported plan, and verify each is refused without writes
open_points.default_guess: Cover all three clauses independently and verify no partial writes.

open_points.subject: INV-025 linking behavior and Required test
open_points.text: A18 says a “violating input is refused and changes nothing,” while State 1 says an unmatched source section creates a new `PortalSection`; neither text defines a same-display-name/different-`source_key` publication as invalid input.
open_points.question: When an incoming section has the same display name as an existing section but a different `source_key`, must linking create a distinct section or refuse the linking operation?
options: Treat it as unmatched and create a new `PortalSection` without linking by name
Refuse the linking operation and write nothing
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as unmatched and create a distinct section, while asserting that the existing section was not reused by display name.

witness.initial: A project has a PortalSection with source_key `k1` and display name `Kitchen`. A candidate snapshot contains a section with source_key `k2` and display name `Kitchen`.
events: The budget-linking operation processes the candidate snapshot.
outcomes: It creates a new PortalSection for `k2`, because only equal source keys link.
It treats the repeated display name as a violating input, refuses the operation, and writes nothing.
witness.observer: The staff member preparing or reviewing the imported budget version.

open_points.subject: source-supplied datetime acceptance and normalization
open_points.text: “their accepted forms and checks … are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7” does not state which datetime representations are accepted, especially for an offset-naive supplied datetime that does not itself identify an instant.
open_points.question: For `approved_at`, `published_at`, `confirmed_at`, `photo_date`, and supplied credential `expires_at`, are naive inputs accepted as UTC, rejected, or interpreted another way, and which offset-aware forms are allowed before conversion to offset-naive UTC?
options: Require an offset-aware input and convert the represented instant to naive UTC
Accept a naive input and interpret it as already UTC
Allow either form, treating naive as UTC and normalizing aware values
open_points.default_guess: Allow aware UTC/offset inputs and normalize them to naive UTC; reject naive source-supplied datetimes because they do not identify an instant.

witness.initial: No record exists yet for a snapshot publication.
events: A producer submits `approved_at` as the naive datetime `2026-11-08 10:00:00`.
outcomes: The portal accepts it as 10:00 UTC and stores the same naive value.
The portal rejects it because no offset identifies the supplied instant.
witness.observer: The producer receiving the import result.

open_points.subject: CLK-001 witness coverage
open_points.text: CLK-001 requires “a test per operation that reads the current time,” but the only bound checks named are `service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal` and `staff_bootstrap_client_portal`.
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to every other operation that writes or compares current time, including staff and viewer session operations and expiry checks?
options: Bind additional existing checks for every such operation
Replace the per-operation requirement with a smaller explicitly enumerated representative set
open_points.default_guess: Bind a witness check for every operation covered by the invariant.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness
open_points.text: The CLK-002 Required tests item has no `[witness: ...]` binding.
open_points.question: Which existing check asserts the monotonic-source, non-persistence, and no-wall-clock-mixing requirements of CLK-002?
options: Bind an existing viewer-entry rate-limit verification check
Add a named State 8 witness check and bind it here
open_points.default_guess: Bind the viewer-entry rate-limit verification check that exercises the clock source.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 process locality
open_points.text: CLK-002 requires elapsed readings to be “used within one process,” but its Required test mentions only their source, non-persistence, and lack of comparison or mixing with wall-clock values.
open_points.question: What must the Required test show to verify that monotonic readings or derived window state are never transferred between processes?
options: Add an explicit assertion that the rate-limit state and monotonic values are process-local
Remove process locality from CLK-002 if only non-persistence and clock separation are required
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit process-locality assertion to the Required test.

open_points.subject: vulnerability-gate age limits
open_points.text: `max_snapshot_age` and `max_environment_age` are called “deployment procedure values” but no values, units, or rule for selecting them are decided.
open_points.question: What are the two maximum ages that determine whether a deploy starts, and are their boundaries strict or inclusive?
options: Specify fixed durations and define whether equality is accepted
Specify a required deployment configuration source, validation rule, and defaults
Remove age-based admission until the deploy route has a decided policy
open_points.default_guess: Make both required positive deployment settings and accept evidence while `age <= maximum`.

witness.initial: A built image has a passing OSV verdict based on a snapshot and environment observation that are both 30 hours old.
events: The deployment operator starts the service from that image.
outcomes: With a 24-hour maximum, the start is refused as stale.
With a 48-hour maximum, the same start proceeds.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and service users.

open_points.subject: age provenance and current-time source
open_points.text: The new rules compare OSV snapshot and environment ages but do not define which timestamp establishes each age, which current-time source performs the comparison, or the timestamp representation.
open_points.question: From which events are snapshot age and environment age measured, and what clock and representation are authoritative at deploy start?
options: Measure from signed snapshot creation and completed verdict time using the deploy route's UTC wall clock
Measure from snapshot retrieval and image-build completion time
Delegate these semantics to the deploy procedure with an explicit receiving decision and witness
open_points.default_guess: Use UTC instants for verified snapshot creation and verdict completion, compared with one deploy-start wall-clock reading.

witness.initial: An OSV snapshot was created two days ago but downloaded one hour ago; the image verdict was computed one hour ago.
events: The deploy route evaluates a one-day maximum snapshot age.
outcomes: Age is measured from snapshot creation, so deployment is refused.
Age is measured from retrieval, so deployment starts.

open_points.subject: configuration treatment of A32 age bounds
open_points.text: A30 says “the existence of every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound is invariant; its value is configuration,” while A32 calls `max_snapshot_age` and `max_environment_age` deployment-procedure values that are “not portal rules” and says no value enters the specification.
open_points.question: Are A32's two maximum ages configuration bounds governed by A30, or are they outside A30 and its formal invariant?
options: Include both age limits in the configuration policy and its required validation
Add an explicit A30 exception for Factory deployment-route bounds
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit A30 exception because these are Factory deployment controls, not portal runtime configuration.

open_points.subject: dependency security-review scope
open_points.text: The dependency category says its affected scope is only “deploy/requirements.txt (fastapi, pydantic, argon2-cffi, uvicorn pinned),” while changed A32 makes every distribution installed in the image, including pip-resolved libraries, subject to the vulnerability gate.
open_points.question: Does the State 2 security review cover all installed transitive distributions, or only the four direct pins named in its affected scope?
options: Expand the affected scope to every distribution installed in the built image
State explicitly that the review lists the direct roots while A32 governs their complete resolved environment
open_points.default_guess: Expand the affected scope to the complete installed distribution set.
